articles.summary: Four plans move up to Gold as Morningstar analysts find improvements across investment teams, oversight, and costs Morningstar , Inc. (Nasdaq: MORN), a leading provider of independent investment insights, today reveals the 2026 Morningstar Medalist Ratings™ for 60 of the nation’s most prominent 529 college savings plans. The Morningstar Medalist Rating for 529 College Savings Plans is a forward-looking assessment designed to help investors identify 529 plans that Morningstar analysts believe are best positioned to serve investors over the long term. Analysts evaluate the quality of a plan’s investment approach; the people managing it, state oversight, and costs, giving investors a way to compare plans beyond past performance. Plans receive one of five ratings: Gold, Silver, Bronze, Neutral, or Negative. This year, Morningstar analysts assigned nine Gold ratings, 14 Silver ratings, 12 Bronze ratings, 19 Neutral ratings, and six Negative ratings. Gold ratings nearly doubled from five
articles.title: Morningstar Releases 2026 Medalist Ratings for 529 College Savings Plans, With 10 Upgrades and No Downgrades

articles.summary: Share of Gen Z, millennial, and Gen X households projected to cover expenses in retirement could rise 8 percentage points, from 59% to 67% Morningstar, Inc. (Nasdaq: MORN), a leading provider of independent investment insights, today released “ From Access to Adequacy: Modeling Universal Automated Savings ,” a new analysis from Morningstar’s Center for Retirement Policy Studies examining how federal savings policies could help more Americans prepare financially for retirement. Researchers used Morningstar’s Model of U.S. Retirement Outcomes to evaluate a combined policy scenario reflecting ideas under discussion among policymakers and policy experts, rather than a specific legislative proposal. The scenario includes expanded retirement savings access, broader automatic enrollment, periodic reenrollment, and an expanded Saver's Match. Under the modeled policy scenario, 67% of Gen Z, millennial, and Gen X households are projected to have sufficient resources to cover retirement
articles.title: Morningstar Research Projects Universal Automated Savings Policies Could Improve Retirement-Income Adequacy
